newsitem.title: USA: Gap Inc to boost ad spending for growth.
newsitem.headline: Gap Inc to boost ad spending for growth.

text.p: Gap Inc said today that in the face of a difficult retail environment, and soft sales in the men's division of its Gap stores, it will be adding more stores, increasing its advertising and promotional budget, and reducing the variety of goods in its Gap stores in coming months.

The company said its advertising and promotional budget, which totaled 1.7 percent of sales, or about $100 million in the previous fiscal year would be bumped up to about 2.2 percent of total sales in fiscal 1997. The company started national television advertising in April, and expects to run other campaigns later in the year.
Gap also said that it is proceeding to open 275 new stores this year, a record number, and that "significant" square-footage would be involved.
The company also said that shoppers at Gap stores would see changes this fall, including a reduction in the assortment of apparel offered.
Thursday Gap reported earnings for the first quarter, ended May 3, of $84.3 million ($0.31 per share) versus $81.6 million ($0.28 per share) in the year-earlier period.
It said that per share income grew at a faster rate than net earnings largely as a result of the company's share repurchase program.
